name: THE FUNERAL
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE COFFIN
LOOK_AT: My coffin. Pine, with handles and a name plate. I am given to understand I look natural.
The lid is propped against the trestle, waiting for me, like a coat held out by a valet.
Someone has put a cushion in it. I suspect the undertaker, and I suspect he will charge.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing from inside, which is the least I can do.
Nothing.
Nothing yet. That changes shortly, and I am trying not to think about it.

overrides.OPEN: Ahead of schedule. The lid stays shut; the plan requires my absence and I am contractually elsewhere.
overrides.USE: It is in use. By me. Officially. The paperwork is immaculate.

subjects.name: THE NAME PLATE
LOOK_AT: THADDEUS GRUB, it says. Even my death is missing a B. I would complain, but the plate was free and so, apparently, was I.
The engraver gave the G a flourish he could not afford to give the rest.
It will be on the lid, over my face, for the next few minutes of my life. I would have liked it spelled right for that.
LISTEN_TO: Brass. It rings a little flat, which in this town is house style.
A faint ring when the wind catches the lid. Flat, as noted.
Nothing. Brass keeps its opinions about spelling to itself.

subjects.name: THE MOURNERS
LOOK_AT: A respectable turnout for a man of my brief acquaintance. Several are here for the singing. One is here for the will. There is no will.
Nine people have come to my funeral. I have been in Consolation eleven weeks. I do not know what to do with this and I am going to have to get into the box shortly.
One of them is holding his hat over his heart and his other hand over his wallet. He has been to funerals here before.
LISTEN_TO: Shuffling, a cough, and somewhere in the middle of it, genuine crying. I was not prepared for the crying.
Nothing. Nine people, not talking.
A sniff at the back, and then a nose blown into a sleeve with real feeling.

overrides.TALK_TO: A stranger offered me comfort at my own funeral. I said the departed sounded like a fine man, taken too soon. He agreed, with feeling. I am having a very strange week.

subjects.name: REVEREND SOWERBY, OFFICIATING
LOOK_AT: Sowerby at grade-two sincerity, which I paid for, delivering me to my reward. He keeps almost catching my eye and electing not to.
He is preparing to deliver four words for fifty cents and he is preparing thoroughly.
He has a card in his palm with the adjectives on it and is ticking them off as he goes. I am getting exactly what I paid for.
LISTEN_TO: '…a man of music, taken flat…' — he wrote that this morning and is proud of it.
Nothing yet.
'…a man who came among us, and stayed…' — that one was free, I think. He has thrown it in.

overrides.TALK_TO (during the service): He is mid-adjective. Interrupting would cost us both.

subjects.name: THE FLOWERS, WAXED
LOOK_AT: The undertaker's wax lilies, making their weekly appearance. We are old colleagues by now, the lilies and I.
Somebody has wiped the dust off them for the occasion. That is the undertaker's idea of grief, and I find I accept it.
They lean toward the grave, the way everything here eventually does.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. They are beyond all that, as previously established.
A faint tap of wax on wax when the wind finds them.
Nothing. They have outlived everyone they were ever arranged for, and they will outlive me, technically.

subjects.name: THE GRAVE
LOOK_AT: Dug neat, in a good spot, uphill of the seepage — the undertaker does honest work for dishonest occasions. I am oddly touched by the drainage.
Six feet, measured. I am two inches shorter than the hole, which is the first time this town has given me room.
A plank is laid across it for the pallbearers. It looks like a very short bridge to nowhere in particular.
LISTEN_TO: Loose soil trickling back in. The ground, impatient.
A clod falling from the edge, then another. The ground is in a hurry.
Nothing for a moment. Then the wind across the top of it, a low, open note.

overrides.CLOSE: Not yet. There is a man not in that box counting on the delay.

subjects.name: THE HEADBOARD
LOOK_AT: A board, painted while the paint lasted: my name, one date, and HE TUNED. As epitaphs in Boot Hill run, that is generous and accurate, which puts it in rare company.
THADDEUS GRUBB. Frame supplied the spelling and got it right, once, for a grave I am not going to be in.
The paint has run on the D's. My name is weeping slightly, which is more than I expected of it.
LISTEN_TO: Wet paint, drying. My legacy, curing in the sun.
Nothing.
Nothing now. The paint has set. It is official.

subjects.name: GRIEVANCE, IN BLACK
LOOK_AT: Grievance in the hearse harness, wearing black well, as advertised. She has attended more funerals than the Reverend and behaves better at them.
A black ribbon is plaited into her mane. She has allowed this, which is a greater tribute than anything Sowerby will say.
She keeps her head turned a little toward the coffin. I do not think she is fooled.
LISTEN_TO: A slow breath through the nose. Professional composure.
A hoof shifting once in the soft earth, then still.
Nothing. She is standing at attention, and she means it more than the mourners do.

subjects.name: THE ONE WHO KNOWS
LOOK_AT: At the back, not singing: Hob, hat in hand, watching a funeral he knows to be empty with an expression I cannot price. It takes one to know one, I suppose.
The night watchman, standing at the back, in daylight. I have never seen him in daylight.
He has not looked at the coffin once. He has looked at me twice.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing from him. He mourns the way he watches. Completely, and without comment.
Nothing.
Nothing. I have never heard a man be so quiet on purpose.

overrides.TALK_TO (before S2 beat 3): Not here. Not with the whole town watching me be dead.

subjects.name: THE DIRT PILE
LOOK_AT: The dirt that was in the hole, beside the hole, waiting.
A shovel stands upright in it, waiting for a volunteer, and nobody is looking at it.
It is exactly the size of the hole. Nothing is ever wasted at the undertaker's.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Loose earth sliding down its side, rehearsing.
Nothing. It is very patient, for dirt.

subjects.name: THE HATS
LOOK_AT: Every man here has taken his hat off. For me. On the strength of a notice in the Clarion that misspelled my name.
Hats of every class, held against every chest. A hat is the only formal clothing most of these men own.
One man is holding two hats. I would like to know whose the other one is, and I am not going to ask at a funeral.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Nobody fans himself with a hat at a funeral.
A brim being turned in nervous fingers, round and round.
Nothing. Nine hats, held still.

subjects.name: THE SKY
LOOK_AT: Clear, very high and very blue. It is a beautiful day to be buried, if one has to be.
One cloud, keeping to itself over the hills.
I am going to want to remember this sky in a few minutes. I am trying to look at it properly.
LISTEN_TO: A hawk, very high, one long cry.
Nothing up there. The sky is not attending.
Wind, high and thin. The last open-air sound for a while.

subjects.name: BOOT HILL, BEYOND
LOOK_AT: The rest of Boot Hill, rising behind in rows. My new neighbors, keeping a respectful distance.
Ezra Pike is up there, third row, second from the end. I came a very long way to join him.
From here the markers look like a crowd that came early and sat down.
LISTEN_TO: Wind through the grass between the rows.
Nothing. The neighborhood is quiet, as advertised.
A loose board on some marker up the hill, tapping, like somebody keeping time for the service.
